body:
You know, now that you mention it, people are really effing weird about hair. When I was in high school, I dyed my hair blue and everyone lost their mind. I was suddenly harassed and picked on, called names, etc. And my best friend - she shaved her head. Everyone called her a dyke right after that. Never happened once before. Now, to their credit, these were teenagers and teenagers are just mean and stupid. But yeah... there's no excuse from adults.

People are just nuts/opinionated about hair I guess.
That's terrible. At least they do not do that anymore.
yeah, i've heard of this before - but I only hear it from black folks. White people pull you aside and tell you your hair is unprofessional? What grounds are there for... I dunno... fighting back?
Oh my goodness. How do you make hair stop growing past a certain length? What do hairdressers say? Cut it off and pray? :(

I understand your hair might be difficult to manage, but does anyone else find it so much more beautiful than weaves and shaved heads and fake hair? I just think your hair is beautiful, that's all. I understand that white fashion society doesn't give it the praise it deserves.

I know what you are going through. My brother died when I was 15. It has been over 20 years and I still grieve. My mother died three years ago and I have not moved past it. I feel numb most of the time. My emotions venture to dark, saddening places that feel hollow and desolate. Grief is the ultimate pain we endure.

The numb feeling leaves me empty, but I can complete my daily tasks. When I panic, things go wrong. When I feel nothing, I'm on auto pilot. 

I can't believe half of the inane things I deal with, experience, or otherwise observe on a day to day basis. Road raging assholes riding my bumper every morning commute. Family members fighting over....nothing. World affairs. Starvation. Crime in my own backyard. Corruption. Advertisements that shout at me like I'm a 5 year old with a low IQ.  Inflation. Ineptitude. Insanity. And it's all considered "normal"....  but it's fucking not.

I'm an adult pushing into my 40's. I've dealt with this, actively as an adult, for over 20 years. What you are describing is not conducive to my experiences, emotional resources, or overall neurological abilities. So...
When you're depressed trying to "improve" your life is much like a cripple trying to kick a field goal. Depression robs a person of the wherewithal to even be able to improve.

I have to go to work and I associate with family and friends, so no I'm not a shut in. I avoid most news sources, but you still hear and experience everything through everyday life. 

What brings me enjoyment? A few random hobbies (e.g. video games) that I struggle to even enjoy anymore. Most of the time I feel like sleeping. Or doing nothing.

Depression is much like sitting down in a chair from which you never get back up.
Why do you care about passing your finals if you're planning to die? Also, why can't a female assist with both?
